links.outcome: Time-in-note change comparing two ambient scribe products head-to-head and versus control
links.effect: Nabla: -9.5% [-17.2,-1.8] vs control and -7.8% [-15.5,-0.1] vs DAX; DAX vs control -1.7% [-9.4,+5.9], p=.66. Burnout gains were similar across vendors.
links.quote: Nabla users experienced a 9.5% [95% CI:-17.2%,-1.8%] (p=.02) decrease in time-in-note versus the control group and a 7.8% [-15.5%,-0.1%] (p=.05) decrease versus DAX users, while DAX users exhibited no significant change versus control (-1.7% [-9.4%,+5.9%]; p=.66).

links.outcome: Documentation time and burnout measures after ambient scribe use
links.effect: Time-in-note fell only with Nabla. Any scribe reduced task load (-35.8) and work exhaustion (-0.27) and raised Mini-Z (+2.76).
links.quote: Reductions in TL (scale 0-400, TL=-35.8 [-63.7,-7.9]; p=.01) and work exhaustion (scale 0-4, PFI-WE=-0.27 [-0.48,-0.07]; p=.01) were seen with users of any scribe.

links.outcome: Physician-reported clinically significant inaccuracies in scribe-generated notes
links.effect: Clinically significant inaccuracies noted 'occasionally' (Likert DAX 2.7 vs Nabla 2.8; p=.68). One Grade 1 adverse event was reported.
links.quote: One Grade 1 (mild) adverse event was reported, while clinically-significant inaccuracies were noted “occasionally” on 5-point Likert questions (DAX 2.7 [2.4-3.0] vs. Nabla 2.8 [2.6-3.0]; p=.68).

screen.reason: This is a pragmatic randomized controlled trial evaluating the deployment of two ambient AI scribes (DAX and Nabla) versus usual care on physician documentation time and burnout, testing the interventions themselves rather than a specific deployment guardrail practice.
